subject.title: fix(browser): stop screenshot vision-failure fallback from injecting raw base64

question: Should configured browser screenshot vision failures intentionally use Option A text-only recovery, or should OpenClaw retain model-visible screenshot recovery through a new session-safe mechanism?
rationale: This PR removes an existing fallback behavior for configured vision users; source and proof establish the contamination bug, but they cannot decide the product trade-off between session safety and degraded screenshot access.

options.title: Approve Option A text-only recovery
options.body: Accept the branch’s behavior: report the vision failure and staged explicit-share path without placing image data in session history.

options.title: Design Option B session-safe recovery
options.body: Keep model-visible fallback screenshots only after defining and proving a transient delivery mechanism that cannot be retained in recent tool-result turns.

options.title: Pause the recovery-contract change
options.body: Keep the current fallback until browser owners choose a supported degradation policy.

recommendation.title: Approve Option A text-only recovery
recommendation.body: Accept the branch’s behavior: report the vision failure and staged explicit-share path without placing image data in session history.

likelyOwner.reason: Best available low-confidence routing candidate for a repository-level browser recovery-contract decision; no more specific current-main owner was available in the supplied history.
